references.text: God said: "Let there be lights in the sky to separate the day from the night. They shall serve as signs for fixed times, and for days and years."
I establish my covenant with you: Never again will all flesh be cut off by a flood, and never again will there be a flood that destroys the earth.
You have set all boundaries on the earth; summer and winter, you have created them.
For this is like the waters of Noah to me: As I swore that the waters of Noah would no longer flood over the earth, so I swear that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
Thus says the Lord: If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night do not come at their appointed time,
They did not say in their hearts: Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives rain in its season, both autumn rain and spring rain, and who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.
Yet he did not leave himself without witness, but did good and gave you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.
Connects God's promise of the permanence of natural laws with reflection on human mortality in relation to the earth's enduring stability.
Highlights how God's establishment of the earth in the Psalms is the theological foundation for the eternal natural laws in Genesis.
Links the original promise of endless seasons with the prophetic restoration of fertility in God's kingdom.
Clarifies that the promise of endless seasons in Genesis is a concrete part of God's eternal covenant mentioned in the Psalm.
